items.title: Sensex, Nifty scale multi-month closing highs as tariff fears ease
items.description: Indian equities saw gains as the market reacted to proposed US tariffs while investor sentiment remained optimistic. The Sensex and Nifty ended higher, approaching levels not seen since early January. Analysts noted the potential for reduced tariffs if a trade deal is reached between the countries. Concerns primarily affected specific sectors such as textiles and shrimp companies with high US exposure.

items.title: Select bluechips drive Nifty rally as market breadth weakens
items.description: India's equity market has shown a rally in November, yet the breadth has weakened significantly amid declining stocks. Analysts note that gains are primarily driven by large-cap blue-chip stocks, with mid and small caps lagging. Recent foreign investments focus on liquid index heavyweights like private banks and FMCG. The overall market breadth has declined in several indices, indicating a potential shift is needed.

items.title: JPMorgan sets 2027 Nifty target at 29,000, sees 12% upside
items.description: JP Morgan has set a target of 29,000 for the Nifty by the end of 2027. This projection reflects a potential 12% increase from the current level of 25,884.50. A strong appeal for Indian equities may arise from broad-based economic growth and scale. Foreign investors could significantly boost inflows if they align with India's index weight. However, several factors may limit further gains in the market.

items.title: These large- and mid-cap stocks have upside potential of more than 21% in 1 year, according to analysts
items.description: It is during a phase when there is a recovery happening in the market that investors tend to make two mistakes. The first is borrowing to invest, and the second is going with the flow. Both seem the right thing to do when the bulls are on the move. Yet they can do real damage when there is even a normal correction.

items.title: Amal Parikh, Puneet Bhatia to raise $1-billion PE fund
items.description: Amal Parikh and Puneet Bhatia are set to launch a substantial $1 billion private equity fund through Avarta Capital. With Parikh taking on the role of managing partner and Bhatia offering guidance while still with TPG Capital, their focus will span across consumer, healthcare, and financial services. They aim for impressive annualized returns of 20-25%, having already garnered ₹7,500 crore in soft commitments, with a target to finalize by March.

items.title: Stocks in news: Tata Group companies, NSE, BSE, Zydus Lifesciences and KPI Green Energy
items.description: Thursday saw Indian equity benchmarks wrapped up firmly, driven by advances in the IT, real estate, and capital markets sectors. As the market gears up for Friday, critical corporate events become pivotal, particularly as Tata Group trusts seek legal intervention against N. Chandrasekaran's reappointment as executive chairman. In a strategic move, the NSE has gained approval to introduce futures contracts on corporate bond indices.

items.title: D-St set for a negative opening as GIFT Nifty signals weak start
items.description: Benchmark Nifty closed marginally higher in Thursday's trading, with broader markets showing better performance overall. IT stocks led the gains, particularly Wipro, Infosys, and HCL Technologies, rising over 3%. Foreign portfolio investors net purchased shares worth Rs 5,843 crore, while domestic institutional investors were net sellers. The rupee settled lower against the US dollar amid rising crude oil prices.

items.title: Sebi may examine Tata Steel-APL Apollo deal amid investor concerns
items.description: Tata Steel plans to acquire a controlling stake in APL Apollo Tubes while selling its steel-related businesses. Stakeholders have raised concerns about the deal's governance and its potential impact on minority shareholders. APL Apollo's largest institutional investors have expressed their discontent regarding the structure and debt implications. The arrangement involves multiple transactions affecting ownership and business structure within APL Apollo.

items.title: Stock Radar: Lupin stocks showing signs of bottoming out after falling over 20% from highs; time to buy?
items.description: Lupin shares have fallen over 20% from their July 2026 high but appear to be forming a strong base around Rs 1,800-1,900. Technical analysts see signs of a potential recovery, with a target of Rs 2,250-2,460 over the next 3-4 months. What should short-term traders do now?

items.title: NBFC credit growth tilts towards retail
items.description: Non-bank financial companies increasingly turned to retail borrowers for lending as industrial credit demand decreased. Retail loans made up 57% of incremental NBFC lending in FY26, showing a significant increase from the previous year. Industrial lending saw a notable decline, particularly in the power sector, which affected overall credit growth. Gold-backed lending contributed strongly to this shift, influenced by rising gold prices. Retail credit growth for NBFCs reached 29.

items.title: SC asks HDFC Bank, three others to ok staff prosecution
items.description: The Supreme Court has ordered HDFC Bank, ICICI Bank, Sammaan Capital, and PNB Housing Finance to grant prosecution sanctions. This order pertains to allegations concerning fraudulent subvention schemes involving real estate developers and financial institutions. Homebuyers were subjected to loan recovery proceedings, even when builders failed to meet their financial obligations. The banks must comply within a week or their heads will have to appear in court.

items.title: Strand Life eyes market share in multi-cancer early detection
items.description: Strand Life Sciences, backed by Reliance Industries, is focused on expanding its CancerSpot screening test capabilities. The company seeks to lower the testing cost significantly over the next two years, targeting below ₹10,000. Reliance's goal includes making advanced diagnostics accessible to a larger population in India. Achieving this requires innovation and development of local genomic capabilities in technology and reagents.

items.title: Private fuel retailers post sales decline in October
items.description: Private fuel retailers, such as Reliance-BP and Nayara Energy, saw substantial declines in diesel and petrol sales. Higher fuel prices led customers to prefer state-run retail outlets like Indian Oil and Bharat Petroleum. As a result, state-run retailers increased their diesel and petrol sales significantly during October. The increase in demand from bulk customers also impacted the market dynamics in October.

items.title: SC suggests Sarfaesi Act update for clarity on creditors' priority
items.description: The Supreme Court has suggested that Parliament amend the Sarfaesi Act for better creditor recovery clarity. This recommendation comes as a response to ongoing conflicts with the Maharashtra Protection of Interest of Depositors Act. The court highlighted that uncertainty has led to prolonged litigation between secured creditors and depositors. In a recent case, the Supreme Court granted interim relief to the State Bank of India.

items.title: HDFC Bank to bring key digital apps in-house amid rising third-party risks
items.description: HDFC Bank is insourcing its digital banking platforms, including MyCards and PayZapp, to strengthen cybersecurity. The transition comes after several cyberattacks have raised concerns in the financial sector. The bank aims to develop and maintain approximately 60-70% of its key applications internally in the near future. This move follows regulatory issues linked to technology gaps in previous operations.

items.title: Ion Exchange India among 6 stocks hitting 52-week low; shares slipped up to 20% in a month
items.description: On Friday, the benchmark Sensex fell 989 points to close at 83,339. Amid the market decline, six stocks from the BSE 1000 Index touched fresh 52-week lows, hitting their lowest price levels in the past year. A 52-week low refers to the lowest price at which a stock has traded over the past year and is commonly used as an indicator of its recent price performance.

items.title: RBI may surprise markets with 50-bps rate hike in December as inflation risks mount: Nomura
items.description: Nomura expects the RBI to deliver a 50-bps repo rate hike on December 4, double its earlier forecast, citing rising food prices, higher core inflation and resilient growth. The brokerage sees a 60% probability of the larger hike, which could take the benchmark rate to 6%, surprising bond markets.

items.title: BEML shares jump 17% to hit 52-week high amid rally in defence stocks
items.description: BEML shares rallied nearly 17% to hit a fresh 52-week high as defence stocks advanced on Friday. The Nifty India Defence index gained 3%, with most constituents trading higher. Omnitech Engineering also hit its upper circuit after securing a development order from BrahMos Aerospace for metallic airframe components and canister subsystems.

items.title: BEML, Data Patterns, Solar Industries, other defence stocks rally up to 11%. What Choice analysts are saying
items.description: Defence stocks rallied, pushing the Nifty India Defence index up more than 3%, led by BEML, Data Patterns, Solar Industries and Paras Defence. The gains came amid a broader recovery in sector revenue growth in Q2FY27. However, Choice Institutional Equities noted that improved revenue has yet to translate into stronger earnings quality, with private defence firms reporting better profitability while defence PSUs continued to face margin pressure.

items.title: Mahanadi Coalfields gets Buy rating from Anand Rathi on listing day. Check target price
items.description: Mahanadi Coalfields received a Buy rating from Anand Rathi with a target price of Rs 165 on its listing day. The brokerage cited cost leadership, e-auction growth, strong coal demand and dividend potential.

items.title: Mahanadi Coalfields shares gain 2% after weak listing. Should you buy, sell or hold the stock?
items.description: Mahanadi Coalfields shares recovered after a weak market debut but continued to trade below the IPO price. Anand Rathi initiated coverage with a Buy rating and a target price of Rs 165, citing strong coal reserves, cost leadership, healthy dividend prospects and rising demand for non-coking coal over the long term.

items.title: From attracting FIIs to starting Demat 2.0 accounts, Sebi chair Tuhin Kanta Pandey lists 4 priorities
items.description: SEBI plans to slash foreign portfolio investor (FPI) onboarding time from several months to as little as five business days and has proposed scrapping the Additional Disclosure Framework for FPIs to align India's rules with global standards. Chairman Tuhin Kanta Pandey outlined four priorities, including simplifying regulations.

items.title: Watrana Rentals shares jump 3% after listing at a discount on NSE SME
items.description: Watrana Rentals shares made a muted debut on the NSE SME platform, listing at a 1% discount to the IPO price before recovering to trade higher. The Rs 120.10 crore IPO saw strong investor demand, attracting bids across retail, institutional and non-institutional investor categories.

items.title: Sebi chairman says looking into Tata Steel-APL Apollo deal to protect minority shareholders; shares rise 4%
items.description: Sebi is examining Tata Steel’s proposed acquisition of APL Apollo Tubes amid concerns over the deal structure and minority shareholder interests. Institutional investors and proxy advisory firms have questioned whether the transaction unfairly shifts debt and risks to public shareholders while benefiting the promoter. The proposed deal could give Tata Steel a 52.38% stake and control of APL Apollo.

items.title: Hindustan Zinc shares gain 3% as silver prices stage recovery
items.description: Hindustan Zinc shares rose tracking a recovery in silver prices, with MCX silver futures gaining nearly 4% to Rs 1,51,439 per kg. Silver has fallen more than 60% from its January peak above Rs 4 lakh per kg, weighed down by expectations of further US Fed rate hikes, equity market volatility.

items.title: India’s rare earnings upgrade: Jefferies names 9 stocks, with Reliance and JSW Steel among its top picks
items.description: Jefferies has turned more optimistic on India's earnings outlook, marking only the third annual upgrade in two decades. The brokerage has named nine preferred stocks, including ICICI Bank, SBI, Bajaj Finance, Reliance Industries and JSW Steel, as FY27 earnings estimates rise on stronger revenue growth and improving corporate performance.

items.title: Global AI selloff hits India: 15 stocks that once rallied up to 400% lose big in reversal
items.description: Indian firms linked to AI infrastructure have seen significant stock price declines, despite the Nifty index's rise. Since October 8, these stocks have suffered due to fears over their valuations and rising capital expenditures, contributing to a worldwide tech stock selloff. Nevertheless, analysts suggest potential in businesses focused on power generation and infrastructure. This moment is viewed as a valuation reset for AI investments, not a complete failure.

items.title: Waaree Renewable Technologies shares surge up to 14% after winning 120 MWp EPC order
items.description: Waaree Renewable Technologies shares rally over 13% after securing a 120 MWp turnkey solar project. The company also announced a Rs 79 crore transfer of project rights by its subsidiary, Sunsational Solar.

items.title: Black Friday Sale! Sensex tanks 1,000 pts, Nifty ends below 25,650 after 2-day rally. 4 key triggers behind selloff
items.description: After a substantial rally earlier this week, Nifty and Sensex encountered losses driven by profit booking. Significant selling arose in major sectors such as banking, IT, and FMCG, although the broader market remained resilient with gains in Midcap and Smallcap indices. Nevertheless, IT stocks faced declines after their recent surge, while rising oil prices sparked concerns over supply disruptions following attacks on Saudi oil facilities.

items.title: Nifty rallies over 10%, but microcaps miss the party: 200 stocks fall, losses touch 42% since September peak
items.description: Microcap stocks have notably underperformed compared to larger indices, suffering significant losses since September. Among over 200 impacted stocks, Jeena Sikho Lifecare experienced the most considerable dip at 42.17%. Experts suggest this trend stems from reduced earnings visibility and liquidity issues. However, certain microcap stocks like Senco Gold and Kitex Garments may offer potential investment opportunities. Investors should stay vigilant by monitoring quarterly results and relevant technical metrics.

items.title: HDFC Bank, SBI, 8 other stocks JPMorgan is bullish on as markets gear up to enter 2027. See full list
items.description: Indian equities enter 2027 with support from improving corporate profitability, easing oil prices, resilient consumer demand, strong domestic credit growth, and a broadening private capex cycle. However, elevated valuations, domestic policy headwinds, and global uncertainties may limit further gains, reinforcing the need for a selective, disciplined, and risk-aware approach. Here are 10 stocks that JPMorgan is bullish on.
